published_prior_art.cite: NabiGuoLiu2026VermaEfficiency: exact single-constraint/mean-scale projection geometry is known; this proposes a specialized explicit multivalued full-arm operator.

GuoLiuBenkeserNabi2026Napkin: continuous-Z optimization is restricted to prescribed finite weighting families; the stated global-vs-finite frontier is a useful but largely variational consequence once Theorem 1 holds.
GuoLiuBenkeserNabi2026Napkin and Cattaneo2010Multivalued do not give a zero-contrast-arm gain iff criterion or nondegenerate mean-Verma witness.

CattaneoChandakJanssonMa2024Boundary, CattaneoFarrellFeng2020PartitionSeries, and BelloniChernozhukovChetverikovKato2015Series supply adjacent concentration/series tools but not the stated joint clipped generated-operator construction.

GuoLiuBenkeserNabi2026Napkin, §4.3.2 and p.33, explicitly retains finite-dimensional local optimization for continuous Z and calls global efficiency open; no growing-sieve attainment theorem was found.
No cited paper gives this enriched held-out certificate, although its population projection identity is standard Hilbert-space geometry.
Cattaneo2010Multivalued, Theorem 1 and §6.1, supplies the multivalued-treatment efficient influence-function/bound framework to which this uncoupled reduction returns.

novelty_flags.label: Proposition 2
novelty_flags.one_line: The uncoupled armwise reduction is a sanity corollary of the already-published multivalued-treatment efficiency theory, not an independently novel root result.

soundness_flags.label: ass:noise-floor
soundness_flags.one_line: The cited Newey--Robins source discusses an upper bounded conditional variance for series estimation, not the proposal's uniform positive lower conditional-variance condition; correct the citation or retag and justify this coercivity assumption.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 20--23, Theorem 7 and §4.3.2; p. 33, concluding discussion
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper characterizes the continuous-Z influence-function class, restricts implementation to K prespecified weighting functions, and states that globally efficient continuous-Z influence functions remain an open problem.
The paper proves the single-constraint orthocomplement, gives the mean-scale orthocomplement and projection formulation, and implements finite-dimensional basis approximations for the Napkin example.

source_verification_receipts.locator: §3, Assumption 3 and discussion immediately following it
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The source treats cross-fitted spline estimators and notes that a bounded conditional variance helps control series-estimator variance; it does not impose or identify a uniform positive lower conditional-variance assumption.
The publication establishes the cited DML/cross-fitting framework for approximately orthogonal scores and valid inference.
The paper develops boundary-adaptive local-polynomial conditional-density estimators with pointwise and uniform concentration and distributional results.
The paper establishes large-sample, pointwise, and uniform results for partitioning-based series estimators, including splines and piecewise polynomials.

source_verification_receipts.version: preprint corresponding to Journal of Econometrics 186(2), 2015, pp. 345--366
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The work develops sharp matrix laws, L2 and uniform series rates, and weaker growing-dimension conditions for least-squares series.
The paper proves sieve-Wald/QLR inference, plug-in estimator asymptotic normality, and sieve variance-estimator consistency for conditional-moment models.
The paper studies fixed finite multivalued treatments under ignorability and derives the efficient influence function and semiparametric efficiency bound for marginal mean treatment effects.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace the Newey--Robins citation for ass:noise-floor with a source that explicitly uses a variance lower bound, or retag it as a novel coercivity condition and explain why it is empirically plausible and indispensable.
Move Proposition 2 to a labeled sanity corollary rather than presenting it as a standalone novelty result; retain its software-falsification role without claiming a new armwise efficiency theorem.

State a direct embedding of Guo et al.'s prescribed continuous-Z weighting class into the proposed full-arm Hilbert class and show a concrete strict-separation law beyond the odd-h inactive-arm example.

Prove the boundary/clipping/fallback concentration event with explicit constants and verify that its operator perturbation remains dimension-free through the Galerkin inverse; this is the load-bearing field-tier attainment step.

recommended_next_step: Revise the unsupported noise-floor citation and demote Proposition 2 to a sanity corollary, then advance the retained full-arm attainment and inactive-arm-frontier kernel to Stage 0.
